editorial:
If you have ever watched a movie and felt the music give you goosebumps, this documentary is for you. Ennio takes you deep into the life of Ennio Morricone, the man behind some of the most famous movie scores ever made. You get to see how he grew from a young trumpet player in Rome into the composer behind classics like The Good, the Bad and the Ugly and The Mission. The film is packed with interviews from big names like Quentin Tarantino and Clint Eastwood, who share stories about working with him. The pacing is steady and never boring, mixing old footage with new interviews in a way that keeps you hooked. You will walk away with a new respect for how much music shapes a movie.

The best part is how personal it feels. You learn about his struggles, his family, and the moments that almost made him quit. The downside is that it runs a bit long, and some sections feel repetitive if you are not already a fan of film scores. Still, the music alone makes it worth your time. If you love movies, music, or both, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The final scenes show Morricone reflecting on his long career and the music he still wants to create. He talks about how every score was a new challenge and how he never wanted to repeat himself. The film ends with a tribute to his lasting impact, showing clips of audiences around the world moved by his work. There is no big twist, but the emotional payoff comes from seeing how one man's music touched millions of lives across decades of filmmaking.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves movies, music, or behind-the-scenes stories about creative legends.
